No, the pedestrian will almost certainly not prevail, because he did not rely on the statement and suffered no loss from it: he rejected the $1,000 offer and won a $550,000 verdict. The statement is also a misstatement of law, which courts generally do not treat as actionable misrepresentation, though some recognize an exception for knowing falsehoods by a party with superior legal knowledge. The shared note is wrong that misrepresentation requires a special duty of trust, since a knowingly false statement of fact can support a fraud claim against an arm's-length adjuster, so the claim fails on reliance and damages rather than on the lack of a duty.

CONFIDENCE: 85
